question: What is the single discount equivalent to three successive discounts 10%, 15% and 20%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying Factors for 10%, 15%, and 20% discounts are 0.9, 0.85, and 0.8.

Combined Multiplying Factor = 0.9 × 0.85 × 0.8 = 0.9 × 0.68 = 0.612

Equivalent Single Discount = 1 − 0.612 = 0.388

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Successive discounts d₁ = 10%, d₂ = 15%, d₃ = 20%

Formula: Net Selling Price = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100)

⇒ Let the initial Marked Price (MP) = 1

⇒ Price after 10% discount = 1 × (1 − 0.10) = 0.9

⇒ Price after 15% discount = 0.9 × (1 − 0.15) = 0.9 × 0.85 = 0.765

⇒ Price after 20% discount = 0.765 × (1 − 0.20) = 0.765 × 0.8 = 0.612

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) = 0.612

⇒ Equivalent Single Discount = MP − SP = 1 − 0.612 = 0.388

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula for Two Rates

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is (x + y − (x × y)/100)%.

Successive Percentage Change

The order in which successive discounts or percentage increases are applied does not change the final result.

Relation between MP and SP

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100 × ... where Dₙ are successive discount percentages.</p
